meta.title: Our Aquarium Leaflet
meta.textType: functional: a leaflet for a trip

paragraphs: On Monday, November second, Teacher Kim brought some leaflets to the classroom. "I have something special for the Explorers," she said. She gave each child a leaflet about the town aquarium. "Our trip is on Saturday, November fourteenth." On the front, a blue shark swam above the words "Discover the Sea." Lily, Mia, Leo, and May sat at their desks and opened their copies. "There is a lot of information here," said Lily. "Please read it, and then ask me your questions," said Teacher Kim.

Inside, the leaflet gave the opening days and hours. "The aquarium is open from Tuesday to Sunday, from nine o'clock to five o'clock." "Buy your tickets at the entrance." "Children: sixty baht per person." "Adults: one hundred twenty baht per person." "Every guest gets a map, including children." "Feeding shows: ten o'clock and two o'clock." "On Sundays, a keeper gives a tour at eleven o'clock." Leo asked, "How much is a ticket for a child?" "Sixty baht," said May, and she wrote the number in her notebook. "How much is a ticket for Teacher Kim?" asked Leo. "She is an adult, so she pays one hundred twenty baht," said May. Teacher Kim laughed. "I want a map, too."

Mia turned her leaflet over. "How long is the shark tunnel?" she asked. Lily read, "The shark tunnel is thirty meters long." Lily read on, "Sharks swim over the guests' heads, so it is a special place." Two rules were at the bottom of the page. "Guests must not touch the glass." "No food in the tunnel." "No food?" asked Leo. "Not even one banana?" "Not even one banana," said Teacher Kim, "but you can eat at the cafe." Lily read, "Indoors: the jellyfish room and the cafe."

"How many hours is the aquarium open?" asked Teacher Kim. "Eight hours," said Mia, "from nine o'clock to five o'clock." "We must stay together as one group," said Teacher Kim. May read the last line, "Please leave by the exit next to the shop." "Our trip is on Saturday, so we cannot take the Sunday tour," said Leo. "But we can watch a show," said Lily.

"I want the first show," said Leo. "The fish eat at ten o'clock, and I am hungry then, too." Mia circled "ten o'clock" with a pencil. "How many shows are there?" asked May. "Two, one in the morning and one after lunch," said Lily. "On Thursday, we will make our plan in the club hour," said Teacher Kim. Lily smiled. "I think this will be a very good trip," she said.
